description: The N>>500 route: run a read-only query against the configured Snowflake account and write the result as ONE tab-separated .tsv file at an ABSOLUTE output_tsv_path in the operator's workspace. Returns immediately with a job_id and status 'queued' (D0.3 deferred-completion shape) -- the dispatch returning is NOT the same as the job finishing; the written path, columns, row_count, and truncated flag arrive when the job completes. The path must lie under an operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry (empty config refuses every export). Same read-only rules and override mechanism as run_query, with a higher hard cap: Snowflake's own Python connector documentation imposes no vendor row ceiling, only our own policy. Defaults to 500 rows absent an acknowledged override -- for that common small/default case, run_query has an identical interface with a lower ceiling. To fetch more, pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with an explicit row_limit (up to 50000) -- both are required together, and a row_limit above 50000 is refused rather than silently clamped. Requires sql and output_tsv_path. When the goal is validating that records exist rather than inspecting their content, prefer selecting stable ID columns over email addresses or other PII-bearing fields -- the query decides what columns land in the file.
embedding_description: Export a large read-only Snowflake warehouse query result -- up to 50,000 rows with an acknowledged override, 500 by default -- to a workspace TSV file. Dispatches asynchronously; the path, columns, and row_count land when the job completes. Use when run_query's lower ceiling isn't enough.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). This is NOT the export result -- that arrives separately when the job completes and is delivered as its own message: path (the written .tsv file in the operator's workspace), columns, row_count, and truncated (true when row_count hit the effective limit -- more rows may exist).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued -- do not present job_id/status as the export result. Acknowledge the request is in flight; the TSV handle itself lands in a follow-up message when the job completes. Once delivered: confirm the written path, the row_count, and the column list. The file contains potentially sensitive corporate warehouse content -- name the path for downstream use (open it, feed it to create_spreadsheet_from_files, join it with other exports) but do not inline its contents. If truncated is true, warn that the export hit the effective limit and point to a higher acknowledged row_limit (up to 50000) if more is needed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Export a read-only Snowflake query's result to a tab-separated file in the operator's workspace, up to an acknowledged override ceiling.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: snowflake.invalid_params: missing sql/output_tsv_path, the path's parent directory does not exist, acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not given together, or row_limit exceeded the 50000 hard cap. snowflake.export_path_refused: the path is not absolute, not a .tsv, or not contained under any operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry (an empty export_allowed_roots refuses every export by default). snowflake.read_only_violation: the statement is not a permitted read leader. snowflake.warehouse_suspended: the warehouse must be resumed by an operator-side admin.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: snowflake.invalid_params naming the override pair: pass BOTH acknowledge_default_limit_override=true and an explicit row_limit, or neither (for the 500-row default); a row_limit above 50000 is refused outright, not clamped. snowflake.export_path_refused: pass an ABSOLUTE path ending in .tsv under a configured workspace root; if export_allowed_roots is empty, add the operator's export directory to the snowflake_plugin config (profile/config/plugins/snowflake_plugin.json) and reload the plugin config. snowflake.invalid_params with a missing-parent message: create the parent directory first. snowflake.read_only_violation: submit a single read-only statement.
